Input-conditioned gating has substantial precedent. [Highway Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.00387) use sigmoid transform gates, commonly with complementary carry gates and negative bias favoring identity propagation. The proposed update instead keeps an unconditional identity shortcut and gates only the residual. [WaveNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.03499) combines conditioned sigmoid gates, causal dilated convolutions and residual connections; [gated convolutional language models](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/dauphin17a.html) use GLUs to provide a linear gradient path. Thus, input-conditioned residual modulation is established; potential novelty lies in the particular conditioning features and normalization, requiring narrower comparison and empirical evidence.

[ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) uses an input-independent scalar initialized to zero: exact identity initialization, with residual-branch parameter gradients initially zero. [LayerScale](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.17239) uses input-independent per-channel scales initialized small: approximately identity, with initially attenuated branch gradients. Neither has sigmoid saturation. By direct calculation, the proposed g=σ(Wx+b)/σ(2), x=[h;u;e;gap;available], gives g=1 at W=0,b=2, preserving the existing h+u block exactly when inserted without other changes. It preserves the baseline function, not identity or guaranteed dynamical isometry; its initial input Jacobian is the baseline I+Jᵤ.

The same calculation gives ∂g/∂z=1−σ(2)≈0.1192 initially, and 0<g<1/σ(2)≈1.1353: strong suppression but only modest amplification. Positive bias reduces gate sensitivity; either sigmoid tail can saturate. Nevertheless, the residual branch initially receives its full baseline gradient, gate weights can immediately learn, and gate-mediated gradients into conditioning features initially vanish because W=0. The identity shortcut remains available, but cannot guarantee well-conditioned gradients once residual and gate Jacobians interact.
